protocol.py: VERIFIED against plate map pcr-03. 96 of 96 wells hold what the plate map says.
  Destination: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4). Reading of the request: full plate.

Labware for the technique (PCR setup): 1 finding.
1. WARNING LABWARE-FOR-TECHNIQUE: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is
  a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
   line 39:  p20.dispense(2, pcr_plate[name])
   The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as
     its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4,
     load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is
     drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the
     reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the
     map verifies; the plate is the problem.
   Affected: wells A1, A10, A11, A12, A2, A3, A4, A5 and 88 more in slot 4.
   Fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips
     on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.
   Source: Opentrons, module setup: no error for an unusual labware and module combination
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/setup.html
   Source: Opentrons, thermocycler: takes the 200 ul full-skirt PCR plate
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/modules/thermocycler.html
   Source: ABC-Bench (Liu et al. 2026): wrong labware identifiers, the commonest LLM error
           https://arxiv.org/html/2606.11150v1
   [6e7561607460]

labware.title: The wrong kind of plate: NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat is a flat plate, and PCR setup needs a PCR plate or PCR strips
labware.explanation: The plate map says the technique is PCR setup, which needs a PCR plate or PCR strips as its destination. The protocol delivers into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot 4, load name nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat), which is a flat plate. A thermocycler block is drilled for thin-walled 0.2 ml PCR wells; a flat plate does not fit in it, so the reaction can never be run. Every well still holds what the plate map asks for, so the map verifies; the plate is the problem.
labware.fix: Load nest_96_wellplate_100ul_pcr_full_skirt (or the 200 ul PCR plate, or PCR strips on the aluminium block) as the destination; a flat plate cannot go in a thermocycler.

protocol.py: 3 biology problems (1 warning, 2 notes).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (well A1 in slot 2)
   line 41:  p20.aspirate(18, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 41 the tip went into master mix (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried
   template (well A1 in slot 3), template (well A2 in slot 3), template (well A3 in slot 3),
   template (well A4 in slot 3) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did it 96
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew
   from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose
   anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the
   next run.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 41 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [33f56091bf75]

2. NOTE NO-SAMPLE-INTO-REAGENT-WELL: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a
reagent
   line 41:  p20.aspirate(18, reservoir["A1"])
   At line 41 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 2 while it still carried
   template (well A1 in slot 3), template (well A2 in slot 3), template (well A3 in slot 3),
   template (well A4 in slot 3) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did it 96
   times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A
   reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every
   reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the
   next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well
   that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted.
   Affected: well A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 41, or add the reagent to the wells first,
   while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling

3. NOTE NO-NEGATIVE-CONTROL: No no-template control: 96 wells of master mix with a sample
   line 43:  p20.dispense(18, pcr_plate[name])
   At line 43 the robot starts putting master mix into NEST 96 Well Plate 200 µL Flat (slot
   4), and 96 wells end holding it together with a sample. No well on this plate holds the
   mix without a sample, so there is no no-template control. If a reagent is contaminated,
   or the primers pair with each other, every well gives a signal and nothing on the plate
   can tell that from a real one. Wells: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 88 more in
   slot 4.

   the template, and tell the plate map where it is.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: master mix (well A1 in slot 2)
findings.explanation: At line 41 the tip went into master mix (well A1 in slot 2) while it still carried template (well A1 in slot 3), template (well A2 in slot 3), template (well A3 in slot 3), template (well A4 in slot 3) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did it 96 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so this stock now holds material that does not belong there. The protocol drew from it again afterwards, but only into wells that were given that material on purpose anyway, so this run is not harmed. What is left in the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 41 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: (proposed) A tip that had been in a sample went into a reagent
findings.explanation: At line 41 the tip touched the liquid in well A1 in slot 2 while it still carried template (well A1 in slot 3), template (well A2 in slot 3), template (well A3 in slot 3), template (well A4 in slot 3) and 92 more from an earlier step (this line did it 96 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, and the protocol never transfers that liquid into this well on purpose. A reagent is shared: the master mix, the enzyme or the primer in that well goes into every reaction on the plate. A tip that has been in one sample leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so a sample carried into a reagent well turns up in every well that reagent reaches, and a no-template control can no longer be trusted.
findings.fix: Use a fresh tip for each sample at line 41, or add the reagent to the wells first, while the tip is clean, and the samples afterwards with a fresh tip each.
